page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.2xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 processor using ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each virtual CPU corresponds to a dedicated physical core without simultaneous multithreading. The instance provides 64 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 474 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware acceleration features include hardware AES encryption, though vector extensions such as AVX or AMX are absent given the ARM architecture.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across multi-core and memory-heavy operations, achieving 12,133.23 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,344.0. In-memory processing is supported by uncached memory read bandwidth of 101.11 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 47.4 GB/sec, supporting 9.53 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-thread performance is constrained, as seen in Geekbench single-core results (930.0) and bzip3 decompression (6.72 GB/sec). Large language model token generation is similarly limited.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the r6gd.2xlarge offers high memory density and high-speed ephemeral local storage within an energy-efficient ARM processor envelope. It is particularly well suited for memory-bound applications that benefit from rapid scratch storage, including in-memory key-value databases like Redis or Memcached, transactional database instances, real-time analytics caching, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.2xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 64 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a generous 8 GB per vCPU allocation alongside 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance exhibits balanced multi-threaded compute and solid memory bandwidth, achieving 9.53 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and steady compilation metrics. Single-thread processing speeds and compression throughput are weaker relative to compute-focused architectures, and the platform lacks hardware accelerators like GPUs. With dedicated physical cores and integrated high-speed scratch storage, the r6gd.2xlarge is engineered for memory-intensive production tasks, including in-memory key-value stores, relational databases requiring ephemeral caching, and high-concurrency web services.
